description: SeamlessAlign is a multimodal corpus of automatically aligned speech translations of more than 470,000 hours covering 37 languages.
name: SeamlessAlign
rai:dataBiases: The paper evaluates gender bias and toxicity in the translation models, but does not explicitly acknowledge biases in the SeamlessAlign dataset itself, other than noting that the raw audio is from crawled web data.
rai:dataCollection: Starting with 4 million hours of raw audio originating from a publicly available repository of crawled web data, audio files were deduplicated, downloaded, resampled at 16KHz, and filtered for non-speech data. Audio was then over-segmented using Voice Activity Detection and speech Language Identification. Speech segments were mined against text sentences or speech segments in other languages using a joint embedding space (Sonar) to identify translation pairs.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio files were deduplicated, downloaded, resampled at 16KHz, and filtered for non-speech data using an audio event detection (AED) model. Audio was split into shorter segments using Voice Activity Detection (VAD), labeled with a speech LID model, and over-segmented into overlapping splits. Text data was sentence-segmented.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables the development of massively multilingual and multimodal machine translation systems, which can augment world-readiness by lowering barriers in cross-lingual communication and providing access to information for those with accessibility needs or who speak languages with script variance.
rai:dataUseCases: Training speech-to-speech, speech-to-text, and text-to-speech translation models.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Voice Activity Detection (VAD) model (Silero), speech Language Identification (LID) model (ECAPA-TDNN), audio event detection (AED) model, Sonar text and speech encoders.
